newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania postpones Congo refugee repatriation.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania postpones Congo refugee repatriation.

text.p: Tanzania has blocked a planned voluntary repatriation of Congolese refugees until formal assurances on security and safety are granted by the new government in Kinshasa, a U.N. official said on Thursday.

Lennart Kotsalainen, deputy head of the U.N. refugee agency in Tanzania, told Reuters a scheduled repatriation on Monday of 300 refugees from the Democratic Republic of the Congo was postponed pending discussions between Tanzania and Kinshasa.

"I think it is possible to solve this question soon. Tanzania would like the government of Congo to state that they (Congo) will welcome these people back and that security is assured," Kotsalainen said.
Concern by Tanzanian authorities for the welfare of the refugees lay behind the demand that Kinshasa "clearly comes out publicly on this issue" he said.
The planned repatriation comes amid attempts by the U.N. to investigate alleged atrocities against Rwandan Hutus committed by forces loyal to President Laurent Kabila.

About 100,000 Congolese refugees from the former eastern Zaire are housed in camps in Tanzania's western Kigoma region after fleeing fighting between Kabila's rebel army and soldiers loyal to ousted dictator Mobutu Sese Seko.
The exodus started late last year with refugees fleeing by boat across Lake Tanganyika. They included more than 200 former Zairean soldiers and 600 family members.

Thousands of refugees, mostly from Uvira, are now agitating to return home following an end to hostilities. Refugees living in Nyarugusu camp with a population of more than 47,000, were literally "waiting with their suitcases ready to go."
President Benjamin Mkapa's spokesman, Patrick Chokala told Reuters, the delay in the repatriation was due to "technical matters."
Chokala said government policy was to ensure: "We don't send people home to problems." He said the Ministry of Home Affairs (Interior) was currently working to resolve the issue of repatriation.
"The principal policy is these people should go home. I don't think this (delay) is a big show (problem)." he said.
Tanzania is host to about 400,000 refugees including 300,000 Burundian Hutus who fled violence in the ethnically-divided tiny central African state.
